core_claim: Across 209 chocolate chip cookie recipes scraped from the internet, the strict mathematical 'average cookie' contains 68 ingredients — including bourbon, zucchini, and white pepper — a small edible parable about how averaging anything humans actually make produces a Frankenstein superset, not a typical instance.

edt_01.label: Hook — The most-average cookie has bourbon in it
edt_01.title: The most-average cookie has bourbon in it
edt_01.editorial_notes: The 68-ingredient count and the verbatim 'Chewy and very chocolatey...' quote are load-bearing. Bourbon at 0.019 tablespoons must be exact (do not round to 0.02). 23 single-recipe ingredients must match ana_04.

edt_02.label: But the average cookie is also boringly normal
edt_02.title: But the average cookie is also boringly normal
edt_02.editorial_notes: Top-12 quantities from ana_06 must be exact (3.526 cups flour, 2.979 tsp vanilla, etc.). The 'cliff' from 74.6% (semisweet chip) to 23.9% (baking powder) must be visible in the chart.

edt_03.label: A close look at the ingredient vector
edt_03.title: A close look at the ingredient vector
edt_03.editorial_notes: This is the centrepiece chart — show all 68 ingredients with prevalence on log/log-like scale. The 'cliff face + long tail' shape is the visual argument. 49 ingredients <5% must be visible.

edt_04.label: Where the bakers actually disagree
edt_04.title: Where the bakers actually disagree
edt_04.editorial_notes: The interactive should be a guess-first reveal on the brown-vs-white sugar question (36.8% / 47.4% / 15.8%) — that is the most counterintuitive finding in this section. Bittersweet bakers' 4.4 cups average must be exact.

edt_05.title: The oven hasn't moved in 80 years
edt_05.editorial_notes: 350F at 74 mentions vs 375F at 46 should be visually decisive. The bigram counts (191, 191, 166, 123) are exact.
